text: . Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives like GST Council.Introduced on 1STJuly, 2017, the Goods and Services Tax (GST) marked a significant milestone in India’s tax reform journey. By bringing multiple Central and State taxes under a unified framework, GST gave effect to the principle of One Nation, One Tax and paved the way for a more integrated and streamlined taxation system across the country. The proposals of the GST Council seek to create a more predictable and taxpayer-friendly GST registration framework. Under the next-generation GST reforms last year, the GST council had simplified the earlier four-tier structure of 5 per cent, 12 percent, 18 percent, 28 percent into a two tier structure of 5 percent and 18 percent. Addressing the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi today, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that through GST, the government has transformed a complex web of taxes into a national market.Addressing media after the 58thGST Council meeting in New Delhi, Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said that the Council   recommended removing arrest powers under GST, raising the prosecution threshold from one crore to five crore rupees.Over the past nine years, standardised procedures and rationalised rates have supported greater transparency, accountability and economic growth and strengthened the vision of ‘Ek Bharat – Shreshtha Bharat’.

. India has issued a fresh advisory for its nationals in Saudi Arabia, particularly Umrah pilgrims, affected by ongoing flight cancellations and is coordinating with authorities of the Gulf Kingdom to facilitate their early return. The advisory comes amid escalating tensions in the region due to a series of drone and missile attacks targeting civilian infrastructure by Yemen’s Houthis.The Consulate General of India in Jeddah said its 24×7 Control Rooms in Jeddah and Makkah continued to provide necessary assistance to affected Indians, with support from community associations and volunteers. The mission also said it remained in regular contact with Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Hajj and Umrah and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to address difficulties caused by the flight disruptions, particularly issues concerning visa validity and delayed departures.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives like Jan Bhagidari.Jan Bhagidari, which means public participation, is a core governance model under Narendra Modi government. Schemes that utilize the Jan Bhagidari model include Swachh Bharat  Mission, Catch the Rain, Vocal for Local, and Pradhan Mantri TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyan. Citizens in India had traditionally been treated as passive beneficiaries of government schemes. Jan Bhagidari has brought a change to this and fostered local ownership and behavioural change in people. Prime Minister Narendra Modi regularly highlights Jan Bhagidari as a core pillar of nation-building through his monthly radio program, Mann Ki Baat. In Mann Ki Baat  last month, Prime Minister Modi again highlighted Jan Bhagidari as a driving force for social change, urging citizens to join collective movements like the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan.Talking to Akashvani News, Shivendra Singh, a resident of Prayagraj, spoke about how he and his family and friends believe in Jan Bhagidari and go Vocal For Local during festive seasons.Participation has now become ownership of transformation happening around the country, with the people becoming stakeholders in national development.

. Six people were killed after a passenger train collided with a minibus at a railway crossing in Russia’s Far Eastern Jewish Autonomous Region.According to railway officials, the accident took place when the minibus attempted to cross the tracks despite a red signal. All the victims were occupants of the minibus, while the train’s passengers and crew escaped unharmed.The state-run RIA news agency reported ​that ⁠all the minibus occupants were foreign nationals, but did ⁠not ​specify their ​nationalities.

. The Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games concluded today with a closing ceremony at the Mizuho Park Athletics Stadium in Nagoya, Japan.Around 4,000 athletes and staff from 45 countries and regions participated in the week-long Games, held in Japan for the first time.Double gold medallists Nishad Kumar and Mona Agarwal led the Indian contingent as flag-bearers at the closing ceremony.India finished the Games with a record 114 medals including 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals, surpassing its previous tally of 108 medals at the 2023 Asian Para Games in Hangzhou, China.Para athletics was India’s biggest medal contributor, with 65 medals, including 22 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze. Para badminton followed with 16 medals, including three gold, five silver and eight bronze. India also secured 11 medals in para swimming, seven in para table tennis, six in para archery, five in para shooting, and two each in para judo and para powerlifting.The sixth edition of the Asian Para Games will be held in Doha in 2030.

. Union Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda today said that former Delhi BJP Chief Kedarnath Sahani was as a multifaceted personality whose life and political vision offered valuable lessons.Addressing an event in New Delhi to mark the 100th birth anniversary of former Delhi BJP president and former Governor Kedarnath Sahani, Mr Nadda highlighted his contributions to strengthening the party and taking its ideology forward.He said, Kedarnath Sahani remained committed to the party’s ideology and served it beyond positions of power. Mr Nadda said, Kedarnath Sahani established traditions, systems and a distinct work culture within the party. On this occasion, Delhi BJP President Harsh Malhotra was also present.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal during the next three days. According to IMD, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Mahe are expected to experience heavy rainfall today.MetDepartment has also predicted thunderstorms with lightning and gusty winds over East Rajasthan, Konkan, Goa, Lakshadweep, Madhya Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh today. Similar weather conditions are likely to prevail over Odisha, Rayalaseema, Telangana, Coastal Karnataka and South Interior Karnataka for the day.For Delhi, the Weather Agency has forecast a clear sky today.

. In Men’s cricket, India defeated New Zealand by 4 wickets in the second T20 International at Hagley Oval in Christchurch today to take a two-nil lead in the five-match series.India achieved the target of 181 runs in 19.5 overs losing 6 wickets. For the visitors, Tilak Varma scored highest unbeaten 51 runs off 26 balls. Earlier, Team India’s bowlers restricted New Zealand to 180 runs for 5 wickets in 20 overs. India had won the toss and opted to field.

. The country’s foreign exchange reserves declined by five billion US dollars to 721 billion US dollars during the week ended on 16th October. According to the Reserve Bank of India’s data, Foreign currency assets, the largest component of the reserves, dropped by 5.7 billion US dollars to 591.8 US dollars during the week. In contrast, Gold reserves rose by 706 million US dollars to 105.8 billion dollars. Special Drawing Rights grew by 30 million US dollars to 18.5 billion US dollars. The country’s reserve position with the International Monetary Fund rose 11 million to 4.79 billion dollars.

. In Men’s Cricket, New Zealand were 60 for 3 in 8.5 Overs against India in the second T20 International at Hagley Oval in Christchurch, when report last came in.India won the toss and elected to bowl against host New Zealand. India made two changes, replacing injured Ishan Kishan with Vaibhav Sooryavanshi while Prince Yadav came in for Mayank Yadav. For New Zealand Jacob Duffy came in for Adam Milne.India are leading the series, 1-Nil after winning the opening match. The third T20 match of the five-match series will be played at Wellington on Tuesday.

. French authorities have arrested 135 people and seized a range of weapons during nationwide demonstrations, as protests over living costs, education and political issues spread across the country.Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said there had been no major incident so far, while police described the situation in Paris as calm. Seized items reportedly included metal balls, lead pellets, fireworks, slingshots, improvised weapons, airsoft guns and a katana sword.In Orléans, around 11,000 protesters gathered by noon to oppose the far-right National Rally party’s two-day convention. Demonstrations were also reported in Marseille, Lyon and Lille, with clashes between police and protesters in Lyon.Major museums across Paris shut their doors as France deployed a massive police force ahead of a fresh wave of protests, determined to prevent a repeat of last week’s violent unrest. The previous demonstrations saw widespread looting, torched vehicles and attacks on public buildings, while masked vandals targeted businesses in Paris and other city centres.

. SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey today said that the next wave in retail broking will not come from the big cities alone but will come from towns and villages.Addressing the 16th International Capital Market Convention of Association of NSE Members of India – ANMI, Mr. Pandey said, the best brokers do not just execute trades, they guide. Stating that KYC must be treated as “Know Your Client’s Needs”, SEBI Chairman said a client who understands risks invests wisely and stays invested longer.He further encouraged brokers to introduce investors to choices beyond equity like a bond, or a unit of a REIT or an InvIT.Raising serious concerns that about six in ten investors rely on unregistered  advisers  and  so-called  influencers, Mr. Pandey said SEBI’s campaign “Samajh Se Investing  Simple” has  drawn  over  15  crore views on social media and sent close to 110 crore WhatsApp messages since its launch on 5th October.Urging market participants to treat cyber security as a business priority, not an IT expense, the SEBI chief said a single breach can shake trust across the system.Stating that the International Monetary Fund – IMF  expects India to grow at about 7 percent  this year, which is more than twice the global pace, Mr. Pandey said, the prediction is largely due to the country’s young population, large domestic market and steady reforms.He informed that India’s equity market capitalization stands around 470 lakh crore rupees while Mutual Fund Assets Under Management – AUM stand around 83 lakh crore rupees.With over 15 crore unique investors and a foreign portfolio investor assets of about 74 lakh crore rupees, Mr. Pandey said the aim is to keep building a  market  that  is  simpler,  deeper  and  safer,  for investors and for market participants.In that direction, the SEBI Chief said, the regulator is reviewing  short  selling  and  securities  lending  and  borrowing  to improve liquidity and price discovery.He added that a framework is being developed to lift secondary trading in corporate bonds and another to put in place safeguards to prevent misuse of trading terminals. Mr. Pandey said SEBI is also exploring  an  AI  sandbox,  where  new  tools  can  be  tested  safely.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives like the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam.In 2023, Parliament passed the Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act – Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, marking a historic milestone in its national journey to foster equitable representation of women in public life at all levels of the federal structure. This landmark legislation reserves one-third of all seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies. In his Independence Day address this year, Prime Minister Narendra Modi appealed to all political parties to end decades of delay and swiftly implement the one-third legislative reservation for women in Parliament and state assemblies.Talking to Akashvani News, Rajya Sabha MP from Bihar Dharamshila Gupta said that through this act, the Modi government has paved the way for half of the country’s population to play a decisive role in political and policy-making processes.The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, once implemented, women’s representation will rise substantially in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies. It is a decisive step towards empowering India’s Nari Shakti with a stronger voice in decision-making and a greater role in shaping the nation’s future.

. In Boxing, Aditya has become the first Indian male boxer to secure a medal at the ongoing World Boxing U-19 Championships in Budva, Montenegro.He defeated Italy’s Tommaso Orlando by a unanimous 5-nil decision to enter the men’s 55-kilogram semifinals today. Aditya will face Azerbaijan’s Nihat Gasimov in the semifinals.Meanwhile, Megha Sheokand in the women’s 80-kilogram category and Prachi Tokas in the women’s 57-kilogram category have also reached the semifinals, assuring India of medals in both events.

. India has condemned the attack at a Church in Karak, Jordan, which took place yesterday. The attack resulted in the tragic loss of several innocent lives and injuries to many others.In a statement, the Ministry of External Affairs said that India stands firmly with the Government and the people of Jordan in this difficult hour. New Delhi has reaffirmed its commitment to the fight against terrorism in all its forms and manifestations.It also extended condolences to the bereaved families and wished a swift recovery to those injured in the attack.External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar has expressed deep shock at the incident. He has also conveyed condolences to the bereaved families and wished a swift recovery to those injured.

. The Centre has created 11 crore farmer IDs across the country, five months ahead of the March 2027 deadline. The milestone has been achieved under the Digital Agriculture Mission implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare.The Farmer ID initiative is designed to provide farmers with a unique digital identity, enabling transparent, efficient and timely access to government schemes, bank credit, crop insurance and disaster relief, while reducing paperwork and repeated verification.Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said this today while sharing a video message. The Minister said that the target of creating 11 crore Farmer IDs by March 2027 was set by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and it was achieved yesterday, five months ahead of schedule.Mr Chouhan said that Farmer IDs will ensure transparent delivery of benefits under various government schemes. They will facilitate farmers in accessing bank loans, crop insurance, disaster relief assistance and selling their produce.He added that the initiative will help ensure that benefits reach the right farmers, while the use of modern technology will make farming easier and more efficient. Mr Chouhan congratulated and thanked the officials and employees of the Central Government, as well as the state governments, union territories, and district administrations, for this achievement.The Ministry added that the Digital Agriculture Mission was launched following the Union Cabinet’s approval on 2nd September, 2024. The Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) being developed under the mission is already showing results on the ground.It added that through the Farmer ID-based service delivery system, more than 6 crore farmers across the country have so far received direct benefits under various schemes.Linking a verified farmer database with agricultural services is helping eliminate fraud and the need for duplicate verification. The Ministry furhter stated that it has also improved coordination among government departments and strengthened policy formulation and the monitoring of schemes, making it easier to track their implementation and delivery of benefits.

. Major US stock indices ended lower yesterday as sell-off in tech stocks in the prior session shifted to other sectors of the market. Communication services, Consumer staples, Consumer discretionary, Financials and healthcare sectors were among the major laggards.The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell over 1.2 per cent, the S&P 500 dropped half a per cent and the Nasdaq Composite declined 0.2 per cent.The indices ended on a mixed note for the second consecutive week. During the week, the Nasdaq shed 0.7 per cent, and S&P 500 fell nearly half a per cent.Conversely, the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 0.4 per cent, marking its third straight weekly gain.

. Director General of Health Services (DGHS) has warned against the reuse of single-use medical devices and disposable surgical items in all public and private healthcare facilities.In a letter to Chief Secretaries, Health Secretaries and Directors of Heath Services of all States and UTs, DGHS said that it has come to its notice that certain private and corporate hospitals are reusing various single-use medical devices and disposable surgical Items, particularly in critical specialities such as Cardiology, Nephrology, Oncology, Cardiothoracic and Vascular Surgery, Neurosurgery, and other specialised clinical services.DGHS has observed that such devices and disposable surgical items, after being used for one procedure, are being subjected to sterilisation and subsequently reused, despite being designated for single use only. More from our correspondent:DGHS has said that the practice of reusing single-use devices and  disposable surgical items raises concerns relating to patient safety, infection prevention and control, regulatory compliance, and healthcare expenditure.It has warned that this can also expose patients to significant risks, including cross-infection, device malfunction, loss of performance, and other procedure-related complications.DGHS has asked all States and Union Territories to ensure strict vigilance and effective enforcement against the reuse of single-use medical devices and disposable surgical items.

. In the forex market today, the rupee depreciated by 11 paise to close at 94.94 rupees against the US dollar. The dollar index, which indicates US dollar’s strength against a basket of six other leading currencies, was trading at 101.77 in intra-day trade.
. In the Indian bullion market today, 24-carat gold was 0.7 per cent down at 1,41,630 rupees per 10 grams. Silver shed 2.7 per cent to 1,94,415 rupees per kilogram.

. The India Meteorological Centre (IMD) has said that a well marked low pressure area over Eastcentral and adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal persisted over the region today.It is most likely to persist over the region and intensify into a depression today. It is very likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify further into a deep depression tomorrow and into a cyclonic storm over the Westcentral Bay of Bengal by Monday morning.Under the influence of likely formation of cyclonic storm over the Westcentral Bay of Bengal by Monday and its further intensification, isolated extremely heavy rainfall is expected  over Coastal Andhra Pradesh on Tuesday and Wednesday and  further over Odisha and Telangana on Wednesday.IMD has issued red colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall with isolated extremely heavy rainfall over Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal tomorrow.The Met Department has forecast Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep and South Interior Karnataka will experience heavy rainfall tomorrow. The weather agency has said that thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds is likely over East Madhya Pradesh, and Andhra Pradesh tomorrow.

. In Badminton, two-time Olympic medallist P V Sindhu has entered the final of the French Open after defeating Japan’s Hina Akechi in a hard-fought semifinal at the Arena Grand Paris today. Sindhu registered a 21-10, 20-22, 21-16 win over world No. 22 Akechi in a match lasting one hour and 13 minutes.This is Sindhu’s second BWF World Tour Super 750 final of the season, following her title-winning campaign at the Japan Open in July. Sindhu will face South Korea’s world No. 1 An Se Young in the summit clash tomorrow.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives like the PM Jan Dhan Yojana.Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana has emerged as a cornerstone of India’s financial inclusion journey since its launch in 2014 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. With over 59 crore Jan Dhan accounts, the scheme has grown into the largest financial inclusion initiative in the world. The scheme has provided universal banking access for every household and has become the foundation for direct benefit transfers. It has helped save almost 3.5 lakh crore rupees by plugging leakages in welfare delivery.Addressing the centenary celebrations of Shri Ram College of Commerce in New Delhi last month, Prime Minister Narendra Modi had said that Jan Dhan Yojana has transformed India’s banking landscape and today almost every family in the country is connected to the banking system.As the world’s largest financial inclusion initiative, the scheme is redefining access to banking for millions of underprivileged citizens. The Jan Dhan account holder can avail overdraft facility of up to ten thousand rupees per household.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues.Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives.Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through the FDI Policy.India’s foreign direct investment policy has undergone major reforms over the past decade, with the government liberalising sectoral rules to attract greater foreign investment into the country. The government has progressively liberalised FDI norms in key sectors, including defence, telecommunications, insurance and space. Foreign investment of up to 74 per cent is permitted in defence, 100 per cent in telecom, insurance and Space sector. The country has received a record over 748 billion US dollars in FDI between 2014 and 2025. The number of source countries investing in India also rose from 89 to 112. Addressing the Rozgar Mela in New Delhi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted that today more than one hundred countries are investing in India through FDI.Chief Economic Advisor V. Anantha Nageswaran said that India has opened up several sectors, including space, drones, defence and insurance, to foreign investment.The FDI policy reforms reflect India’s efforts to create a more investor-friendly environment, simplified investment procedures and to strengthen its position as a preferred global investment destination.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will attend the third day of the mega air show, ‘Wings Over Ganges’, at the Namo Ghat in Varanasi today as the Chief Guest. The event is being organised to mark the 94th anniversary of the Indian Air Force. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will also be present on the occasion. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the Reserve Bank of India’s Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute at Jatni, near Bhubaneswar, in Odisha this evening.

. North Korean leader Kim Jong Un today visited China and inaugurated a new bridge connecting the two countries, expressing hope for stronger cooperation with Beijing. Kim reached the Chinese border city of Dandong after crossing the newly opened bridge.He said North Korea was ready to work with China to strengthen their historic friendship and expand practical cooperation for the mutual benefit of the two peoples. Kim’s visit coincides with the anniversary of a key battle involving Chinese forces during the Korean War.Kim last visited Beijing in September 2025, when he met Chinese President Xi Jinping and attended a military parade alongside Russian President Vladimir Putin.

. In Asian markets today, China’s Shanghai Composite rose 0.9 per cent, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng gained 0.7 per cent, South Korea’s Kospi advanced 0.3 per cent, and Singapore’s Strait Times added 0.1 per cent. On the other hand, Japan’s Nikkei 225 lost 0.3 per cent, while markets in Taiwan remained closed for a holiday.On the economic front, Japan’s consumer price index (CPI) rose 2.1 per cent year on year in September, up from 1.9 per cent in August. This marked the first time in nine months that inflation had exceeded the Bank of Japan’s two per cent target.In European markets, Germany’s DAX dropped 0.9 per cent, while London’s FTSE 100 lost 0.6 per cent, when reports last came in.

. In Women’s Cricket, India defeated Zimbabwe by nine wickets in the first One-Day International at Vadodara last night to take a one-nil lead in the three-match series. Chasing a target of 198 runs, India cruised to victory in just 27.1 overs, with nine wickets in hand and 22.5 overs to spare. Pratika Rawal struck an unbeaten 100 off 96 balls, including 15 boundaries, to register her third century in the 50-over format. Earlier, Shree Charani returned career-best figures of four for 23 to restrict Zimbabwe. Beloved Biza was the top scorer for Zimbabwe, with 62 runs off 92 balls.Earlier, India’s bowlers restricted Zimbabwe to 197 runs in 49.5 overs after the visitors won the toss and elected to bat. Spinner Shree Charani led the attack with figures of four for 23. Kranti Gaud claimed three wickets, while vice-captain Deepti Sharma took two and Shafali Verma picked up one. Beloved Biza was Zimbabwe’s highest scorer with 62 runs.Pratika Rawal was adjudged Player of the Match. The victory marked a dominant start for the reigning ODI world champions, who returned to the format after a gap of nearly eight months. It was also Smriti Mandhana’s first ODI as India’s full-time captain. The second match of the three-match series will be played in Vadodara tomorrow at 2 PM IST.

. Airline operator Indigo has said that its flights to and from four Saudi Arabian cities will remain cancelled in view of the evolving security situation till 31st of this month.In a social media post, Indigo said that its flights to and from Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah will remain cancelled till 31st of this month. The Airline said that the safety and well-being of customers and crew continue to guide their decisions.It added, they are in close coordination with the relevant authorities to ensure safe operations.

. President Droupadi Murmu has expressed joy and pride that Indian para-athletes have achieved unprecedented success at the Asian Para Games 2026, with the highest-ever tally of 114 medals.The President said that this extraordinary success, powered by hard work, perseverance and a firm self-belief among Team India has set an example that inspires the young people to remain undaunted by constraints, dream big, work with dedication and always remain positive.In a social media post, she has conveyed greetings to the entire Indian contingent.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives like the semiconductor mission.Semiconductors are the building blocks of modern technology and a foundation of economic power. They power Artificial Intelligence (AI), telecommunications, electric mobility, defence and advanced manufacturing.  In the past two years, the global semiconductor market has grown by more than 20 per cent. 12 semiconductor projects have been approved across six states in the country, with investments commitments of more than one lakh 64 thousand crore rupees. Addressing SEMICON India 2026 in New Delhi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that India is taking every step needed to become a preferred destination for the semiconductor industry.Talking exclusively to Akashvani News, IT Expert Prasoon Sharma said India’s semiconductor journey is no longer a story of aspiration but is becoming a story of execution.India’s semiconductor journey has evolved from building strategic capabilities to creating a broader domestic ecosystem. These efforts are positioning India to participate across the semiconductor value chain.

. A 5.3-magnitude earthquake struck Zadoi County in northwest China’s Qinghai Province today, two days after a powerful 7.0-magnitude earthquake hit neighbouring Tibet, claiming 16 lives and injuring 76.According to the China Earthquake Networks Centre, the latest quake struck at 2:09 PM IST (Indian Standard Time) at a depth of 10 kilometres. No immediate reports of casualties or damage were received from the affected region.Meanwhile, in Tibet, rescue and relief operations continue following the earthquake, with more than 12,400 residents evacuated from affected areas. Authorities have deployed over 2,500 rescue personnel, while relief supplies are being delivered and temporary resettlement sites established to support those affected.The region has recorded 834 aftershocks, including eight measuring between 4.0 and 4.9 in magnitude.

. PV Sindhu has entered the final of the French Open Badminton Championship following a thrilling win over Japan’s Hina Akechi in Paris yesterday. She secured her spot in the final after defeating Hina Akechi 21-10, 20-22, 21-16 in a grueling 73-minute semifinal clash. The 31-year-old two-time Olympic medallist has reached her second Super 750 final of the season, following her title win at the Japan Open in July. Sindhu will face South Korea’s World No. 1, An Se-young, in the final today.

. Saudi authorities today issued emergency alerts warning of a hostile aerial threat in Mecca, Jeddah, Yanbu and Taif. The Civil Defense urged residents to follow safety instructions, avoid gatherings and refrain from filming.It also advised people to call 911 in case of an emergency. Meanwhile, spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition, Major General Turki Al-Maliki, said air defences had intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by Houthi rebels towards the Saudi cities of Taif and Yanbu.In Yemen, fierce clashes have resumed between Saudi-backed government forces and Houthi rebels on the eastern front near Taiz. The fighting involved heavy and medium weapons, artillery shelling and air strikes. These developments come amid heightened security concerns in the region, with attacks targeting civilian and critical infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.

. The fifth edition of Kashi Tamil Sangamam (KTS 5.0) will be held from 28th November to 12th December this year. The programme will celebrate, reaffirm and strengthen the age-old civilisational bonds between Tamil Nadu and Kashi, the two ancient seats of learning, strengthening the spirit of Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat. The Ministry of Education said that the theme of KTS 5.0 is Thirukkural Payilvom – Thirukkural Abhyas Karen.Akashvani correspondent reports that as part of the Sangamam, around 1,400 participants from Tamil Nadu, divided into seven groups of approximately 200 members each, will undertake an 8-day journey. The itinerary will include Varanasi, Prayagraj and Ayodhya and featuring cultural, academic, domain-specific and spiritual engagements. The emphasis on youth participation will enable a new generation to engage meaningfully with India’s classical knowledge traditions. Ministry of Education invites eligible applicants from Tamil Nadu, especially youth and students, to register for the programme and participate in this celebration of India’s cultural oneness, linguistic diversity and shared civilisational inheritance.Interested applicants can register through the official Kashi Tamil Sangamam portal, hosted by IIT Madras, at https://kashitamil.iitm.ac.in/. Registration has commenced on the 22nd of this month and will remain open until the 13th of next month. The Ministry informed that applications are invited under seven categories, including students, teachers, writers and media professionals, agriculture and allied sectors, professionals and artisans, women, and spiritual leaders.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the Reserve Bank of India’s Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute at Jatni, near Bhubaneswar, in Odisha this evening. Built at an estimated cost of 170 crore rupees, the facility is expected to strengthen data security and enhance the resilience of India’s digital financial infrastructure.Odisha is hosting the RBI’s second data centre in the country, marking a significant development in the state’s growing technology infrastructure. The project will also promote specialised training and research in cybersecurity and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and quantum computing. The facility is expected to provide additional capacity for safeguarding critical financial data and improving the resilience of the country’s digital financial infrastructure.The accompanying Cybersecurity Training Institute will serve as a dedicated centre for specialised training, research and capacity building in enterprise computing and cybersecurity. It will also focus on emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence and quantum computing. The initiative assumes significance as India’s digital payments ecosystem continues to expand, increasing the need for secure, reliable and resilient financial systems. The project is expected to strengthen the Reserve Bank of India’s technological capabilities and contribute to the security and stability of India’s financial ecosystem.

. The curtains will come down on the Fifth Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, today, bringing the continental sporting event to a close.Double gold medallists Nishad Kumar and Mona Agarwal will be India’s flag-bearers at the closing ceremony, scheduled to begin at 2:30 PM Indian Standard Time. Both athletes secured two gold medals each in their respective disciplines.Nishad Kumar won gold in the men’s high jump and long jump in the T47 category. With this achievement, he joined para-runner Ankur Dhama and armless archer Sheetal Devi as one of the few Indian athletes to win two gold medals in a single edition of the Asian Para Games.Mona Agarwal, meanwhile, won gold in the women’s 10-metre air rifle standing SH1 event with a Games record. She followed it up with another gold in the women’s 50-metre rifle three positions SH1 event, setting a world record.India concluded its campaign with a record haul of 114 medals, including 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze after a strong final-day finish yesterday. India’s medal tally received a significant boost yesterday, with athletes from para-badminton, archery and shooting contributing to the gold medal count. For the first time at these Games, para-athletics was not India’s leading source of gold medals. The country surpassed the previous edition medal count of 108 medals comprising 27 gold, 32 silver and 49 bronze medals, achieved at the 2023 Asian Para Games in Hangzhou, China.

. India’s business sentiment improved in the July-September quarter of this fiscal year after declining for four consecutive quarters. The Business Confidence Index rose to 107.8 from 99.8 in the previous quarter, according to the latest survey by the National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER).The survey, conducted in September among 502 firms across six cities, found improvement in all four indicators of business confidence. The share of firms expecting overall economic conditions to improve over the next six months rose to 50 per cent from 43 per cent. Expectations of improved financial positions increased to 41 per cent from 37 per cent, while the share viewing the investment climate positively rose to 30 per cent from 26 per cent. Firms expecting capacity utilisation to remain near or above optimal levels increased to 94 per cent from 91 per cent.NCAER survey indicated a broad-based recovery in sentiment among both micro, small and medium enterprises and large firms. The Business Confidence Index for MSMEs rose from 93 to 100, while that for large firms increased from 111.6 to 120.3. She added that business prospects had improved in both domestic and external markets, while cost sentiments had moderated.

. India made a winning start to the Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship in Ahmedabad yesterday. The Indian women’s team defeated Malaysia 73-13, while the Men’s team beat England 46-26.The women dominated from the start. They led 30-11 at half-time and continued their strong performance after the break. Sakshi was the top scorer with 13 points. Captain Nidhi Sharma contributed eight raid points, while Renuka added nine raid points. India inflicted six all-outs on Malaysia without conceding one.In the Men’s match, led by captain Surjeet Singh, India took an early lead and were ahead 23-9 at half-time. Naveen Kumar led the scoring with 12 points, while Neeraj Narwal contributed 11 raid points. England fought back in the third quarter but India regained control in the final quarter. The hosts scored 16 points in the final quarter to seal a convincing 46-26 victory. India inflicted three all-outs on England without conceding one.

. Home Minister Amit Shah has congratulated the anti-narcotics team comprising central agencies and police forces of Assam, Mizoram and Manipur for launching a barrage of simultaneous crackdowns across 38 locations and smashing an international narco-cartel. He said the Modi government dealt another lethal blow against drugs with Operation Trident.In a social media post, Mr Shah informed that the operation led to the arrest of 18 people, revealing 100 crore rupees worth of hawala transactions. He said 1,424 bank accounts have been frozen, properties worth around 18 crore rupees have been attached, and 500 detonators and 12 lakh rupees in cash were seized.The Home Minister said the network trafficked narcotics across the borders of India, Myanmar and Bangladesh through the Death Triangle Corridor. He said the offensive attests to India’s Himalayan resolve to realise the mission of eradicating every drug network by 31st December 2029. Mr Shah reiterated that India will hammer until the last nail is driven into the coffin of drug cartels.

. In the United States, several parts of the country are making voting more accessible through multilingual ballots and interpreter services. As per the media reports, in elections to be held on the 3rd of next month, Chicago offers ballots in Hindi, Gujarati and Urdu at all polling stations, while California and parts of New York also provide language assistance. However, Texas, home to over six lakh Indian Americans, does not offer ballots in Indian languages.The developments highlight efforts to make elections more inclusive, while underscoring the need to further expand language assistance for voters. The United States midterm elections will take place on the 3rd of next month. These elections occur near the midpoint of the current presidential term and will determine control of both chambers of the United States Congress, alongside various state-level positions.

. Global crude oil prices rose today. Brent crude was trading one per cent up at 114 US dollars and 31 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 1.2 per cent higher at 100 US dollars and 70 cents per barrel, at the time of writing this report.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives like Give It Up Campaign.The Give It Up campaign, launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2015, has encouraged consumers to voluntarily give up their LPG subsidies. Under the campaign, more than one crore 13 lakh LPG consumers have voluntarily surrendered their LPG subsidy. The savings helped provide LPG connections to poor households under the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana, particularly benefiting rural women who relied on firewood and cow dung for cooking. The government has provided over ten crore 56 lakh free LPG connections under the scheme to adult women from poor households across the country. Addressing the Delhi Economics Conclave in 2015, Prime Minister Modi highlighted that the Give It Up movement inspired the citizens to come together to help underprivileged families acquire clean fuel.A resident of Uttar Pradesh, Sanju Devi said that the gas stove has made cooking much more convenient and freed her from exposure to smoke.The Give It Up campaign has promoted a sense of social responsibility among citizens and has supported the government’s efforts to ensure clean cooking fuel access for all.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives aimed at removing the colonial mindset.The history of modern India is deeply entangled with two centuries of British colonialism, and decades after Independence. Over the past few years, the Government has slowly been steering India, away from these vestiges of British rule. Addressing the nation from the Red Fort on the 76th Independence Day in 2022, the Prime Minister outlined five resolutions, or Panch Pran for the next 25 years. Elaborating on the second Praan, he said, in no part of citizens’ existence, not even in the deepest corners of mind or habits should there be any ounce of slavery.In a concerted effort to free the country from its colonial legacy and promote a distinct Indian identity, the Government has undertaken a series of initiatives across various sectors. the historic Rajpath in New Delhi was renamed Kartavya Path and inaugurated by the Prime Minister in 2022.  Similarly, a grand statue of freedom fighter Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose was installed near India Gate, which has replaced the statue of King George the Fifth. The Indian Navy also adopted a new ensign in 2022, replacing the earlier design that featured the Saint George’s Cross. The Government has merged the Rail Budget with the Union Budget from budget year 2017-18, ending a practice dating back to 1924. BJP leader Ram Madhav has said that restoring India’s cultural and civilizational identity is a symbol of self-respect. He added that decolonisation is the real patriotism that is happening today.The Government has further sought to revive literature banned during British rule, with the National Archives of India compiling a catalogue of banned poems, writings and publications from the freedom struggle. In addition, more than 1,500 obsolete laws have been repealed in recent years as part of efforts to simplify governance and remove outdated legal provisions.These initiatives reflect the Government’s stated commitment to building a confident, self-reliant India rooted in its cultural heritage and national values.

. Benchmark domestic indices snapped their two-week rising streak dragged by higher crude oil prices due to escalating West Asia conflict. During the holiday-shortened week, the 30-share Sensex at the Bombay Stock Exchange declined 1 thousand 605 points, or 2.14 per cent, to close at 73 thousand 124.The National Stock Exchange Nifty 50 lost 546 points, or 2.35 per cent to end at 22 thousand 600. The sell-off spread beyond large-cap stocks, with mid-cap and small-cap indices experiencing sharper declines as investors reduced exposure amid rising uncertainty.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, Midcap 100 index shed 5.6 per cent, while the Nifty Smallcap 100 index tanked more than 7 percent during the week.Across sectors, IT was the lone pocket of resilience, recovering from early selling to end the week largely unchanged on improving earnings visibility and renewed investor appetite.Among the major laggards, Nifty Defence index plunged seven per cent, followed by the Nifty Consumer Durables index, which fell 6.4 per cent. Investors’ wealth eroded this week, with the total market capitalization of BSE listed companies declining by nearly 21 lakh crore rupees.In the forex market, the Indian rupee appreciated marginally this week to settle at 94 rupees and 94 paise against the US dollar.

. External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar today said that India-Africa partnership is built on shared histories, common aspirations and Deep South-South solidarity.The Minister said this during an interaction with Heads of Mission from Africa in New Delhi. In a social media post, Dr. Jaishankar said that they discussed various aspects of India-Africa partnership, the rise of Africa in a multipolar world, and new possibilities for people-centric cooperation.

. Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan today, claiming one life and injuring more than 500, while bringing down trees, disrupting flights and knocking out power to hundreds of thousands of households.The storm, which had earlier intensified into a super typhoon and ranked among the strongest systems in the Pacific this year, has weakened but continues to pack powerful winds as it moves north towards China’s eastern coast.Taiwan’s fire department confirmed one death after a man was swept away by waves near Liuqiu Island. A total of 527 people were injured amid strong winds and torrential rain. Power utility Taipower said, more than 288,000 households had lost electricity during the storm, although most supplies had since been restored.China’s emergency management ministry dispatched a team to Zhejiang province as Champi approached the country’s eastern coastline, warning of strong winds and heavy rainfall tomorrow.Forecasts indicated that Champi would continue moving north along China’s coast before eventually heading towards southern Japan.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today said Mann Ki Baat has completed 12 years and that the journey has felt like a pilgrimage for him. Addressing the nation through his Mann Ki Baat programme on Akashvani,  the Prime Minister noted that Mann Ki Baat began on the auspicious occasion of Vijayadashami 12 years ago. Since then, this journey has continued without a break.The Prime Minister said that the listeners of Mann Ki Baat are both his fellow travellers and guides. He further said that Mann Ki Baat has been an auspicious opportunity to proudly celebrate the hard work, valour, commitment, dedication, and spirit of service of the common people of the nation. Mr. Modi added that this has been like a Teerth Yatra (pilgrimage trip) to closely understand the efforts of the people and to salute their contributions. He said people who live for society and the nation are, in themselves, like a ‘Teerth’ (Pilgrimage). He also said that through Mann Ki Baat, he is paying obeisance to the collective strength of the people of India.The Prime Minister said that Mann Ki Baat provides him with an opportunity to connect with every family across the country. He said this deep connection and the affection shown by all of the listeners is a priceless treasure. Saying that the nation possesses many traditional skills that have been a part of its identity for generations, Prime Minister Modi highlighted an initiative underway in Punjab. An organisation called ‘Kheti Virasat Mission’ has begun to breathe new life into organic farming and traditional agricultural practices. The team aimed to promote natural cotton cultivation in the Malwa region of Punjab, with the initiative named ‘Nav-Trinjan’.Under this project, organic cotton with natural colours is cultivated, eliminating the need for additional chemicals to dye the resulting yarn or fabric. ‘Nav-Trinjan’ also established a weaving school with the goal of passing on the craft of weaving to the next generation. Mr Modi mentioned how Ramandeep Kaur, a labourer; Suneha Devi, a domestic help and Rajni Kaur, a manual labourer are now being recognised as a skilled- weavers who are supporting their households with this new found skill. He also mentioned that a shawl woven by Rekha Rani has been presented to the President of India. He recalled meeting this team on National Handloom Day a few months ago. He extended his heartfelt wishes to the entire team for a bright future.Speaking about conservation of Nature, Mr Modi highlighted the efforts in Tehri Garhwal region of Uttarakhand to breathe new life into the ‘Heval’ river and the natural water sources in the surrounding area. He commended the local administration and the villagers who launched a campaign to save the Heval river. Measures were undertaken to capture rainwater, facilitate groundwater recharge and plant a large number of trees. Mr Modi noted with satisfaction that due to these efforts, the Heval river has been revitalised and dozens of natural water sources have received help in their restoration.The Prime Minister noted that cleanliness drives are being run at many places ahead of festivals like Diwali and Chhath. He stressed the need to maintain cleanliness of the places where people live. He added that small, individual efforts can bring about significant change in the surroundings.The Prime Minister expressed happiness that people are placing great importance on Swadeshi products while shopping during this festive season. He remarked that this spirit of ‘Vocal for Local’ is taking Indian products to global markets. He highlighted that Makhana from Purnia in Bihar is now reaching Greece, and Arhar Dal from Kalaburagi in Karnataka is being exported to the Maldives. He underlined that new global markets are opening up for Indian farmers.Mr Modi emphasised that packaging of a product is just as significant as its quality. He cited the example of tribal communities in Maharashtra who have placed a strong focus on the packaging of the products they create. Through an initiative called ‘Shabari Naturals,’ products like honey, mahua, chironji and bamboo-based items are being brought to the market with packaging which reflects their tribal art. Mr Modi shared that this packaging has received Japan’s prestigious ‘Good Design Award.’ Prime Minister Modi also spoke about a ‘bamboo’ start-up in Karnataka which is creating packaging material from bamboo and agricultural residue.Mr Modi expressed happiness that on Gandhi Jayanti this year, sales of the products of Khadi Gram Udyog crossed 28 crore rupees in a single day. This is an increase of 1.5 crore rupees over last year. He said the popularity of Khadi continues to grow, and the benefits are reaching the people who bring Khadi and various handicrafts to life. Mr Modi urged people to prioritise products made by local artisans during the festive season. He added that this will further strengthen the ‘Vocal for Local’ movement and the dream of ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’ will be realised sooner.Speaking about the e- Sanjeevani scheme, Prime Minister Modi expressed satisfaction that approximately 50 crore tele-consultations have been conducted through this platform so far to make people’s lives easier. Mr Modi said this serves as an excellent testament to the power of technology, dedication of doctors, and the trust placed in the system by the people. He highlighted that through its extensive network, the ‘e-Sanjeevani’ service has reached even the remotest corners of the country. He recounted some of the stories of those who have benefited from it. In the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Oho-Tahane, from the Jarawa tribe on Baratang Island, was suffering from a high fever.  Local health workers used e-Sanjeevani to consult an expert doctor. The child had pneumonia. The patient’s condition began to improve rapidly once he came under the care of the expert doctor.In Kalpeni, Lakshadweep, a 60-year-old man named Kunhi Koya suddenly fell ill. Through e-Sanjeevani, contact was established with an experienced doctor located across the sea in Kavaratti. The experienced doctor provided guidance to the local medical team, which helped bring relief to Kunhi Koya. In Zanskar, Ladakh, Kunjang Dolma experienced complications during her pregnancy. A specialist doctor provided immediate assistance to her through e-Sanjeevani. In Peren, Nagaland, a 12-year-old boy named Mushem suffered from an ear infection and fever. With the help of e-Sanjeevani, the expert doctor was able to promptly diagnose his condition and recommend the appropriate medication.Mr Modi said there was a time when even a simple health check-up or a visit to a doctor would take a long time and involve significant hardship. He said that today, nearly one lakh ninety thousand ‘Ayushman Arogya Mandir’ across the country have brought new facilities into people’s lives. He added that these Arogya Mandir are in a way, evolving into wellness centres for village panchayats.Recalling his trip to Chennai earlier this month, Mr Modi said he met many of the nation’s scientists, researchers, and young talents. He said the nation’s youth are currently working on subjects that have the potential to transform the future of humanity. He cited ‘Brain Research’ as one such field.  Mr Modi had  inaugurated the ‘Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre’ at IIT Madras. This Centre has developed a brain-imaging technology platform that serves as a global benchmark. Through this, high-resolution, digital 3D images of the human brain are being created, with the goal of mapping and studying 100 human brains in minute detail.The Prime Minister said that this is the first mission of its kind in the world, which utilises the ‘Param Shakti’ supercomputer. He noted that the nation’s industry has played a significant role, in collaboration with the Government, in establishing this Brain Centre. Many IIT alumni and academia have also come together to support this research centre. He highlighted the importance of this project as the human brain remains a major scientific enigma. He pointed out that even in the present day, conditions like Alzheimer’s and Dementia still lack a definitive cure. It has also been decided that this data from 100 human brains will be made available as an open-source resource for research across various fields.Touching upon the subject of organ donation, Prime Minister Modi said it plays a vital role in such advanced research. He gave the example of Shivani from Narmadapuram in Madhya Pradesh who had met with a road accident, and her family decided to donate her organs. Mr Modi praised her family, saying such a step of humanity can bring happiness back into a family’s life, while also providing significant support to research efforts.The Prime Minister also shared some other experiences from his visit to Chennai. The first was his interaction with young people on the metro, while another was his visit to IIT Madras. Mr Modi highlighted that one of the start-ups he met focuses on verifying the quality of gold, which can help prevent fraud in gold purchases. He added that another team is developing a platform that could enable the rapid recovery of funds lost to bank fraud. He further said that another team is exploring how AI can assist in the screening for cervical cancer.Mr Modi said that the interaction at IIT was entirely focused on ‘deep-tech.’ These start-ups are being supported by the incubation ecosystem at IIT Madras. He noted that while one start up is developing an electric vehicle capable of flying over the sea, another start-up is developing fast-charging batteries for drones and electric vehicles. He said one team is working on the application of AI in Defence technology.Prime Minister Modi opined that the youth are achieving such extraordinary milestones today because of the right environment and support. He said that the nation will mark the 100th birth anniversary of great Indian scientist, Narinder Singh Kapany on 31st October. The world knows him as the ‘Father of Fiber Optics.’ He was born in the Moga district of Punjab. Mr Modi said his advanced research into the technology of transmitting light through thin fibres lent a new direction to the world of communication. He paid his respects to Narinder Singh Kapany. He urged nation’s youth to read and learn about scientists like him, and draw inspiration from them.The birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel will be celebrated on the 31st of October. The nation observes ‘Ekta Diwas’ on this day. Prime Minister Modi said a ‘Run for Unity’ is organised across the country on this day. He said ‘Run For Unity’ offers the opportunity to strengthen the nation’s unity and reaffirm  commitment to the nation. He urged everyone to participate enthusiastically in this year’s ‘Run for Unity’.On this episode of Mann Ki Baat, Prime Minister Modi also spoke about millets, highlighting that 2023 was celebrated as the ‘International Year of Millets’ at India’s call. He said it received a very positive response globally. Through this initiative, people discovered how deeply millets are rooted in country’s own culture. Mr Modi said that there has been a rich tradition of millet cultivation in Northeast as well. He said that people had begun to drift away from it but that situation is changing now.He spoke about a village called Khanduli in the West Jaintia Hills district of Meghalaya, where millets have been an integral part of food culture over many generations. The number of farmers cultivating millets had been on the decline for some time. Mr Modi said that two women from the village undertook the new initiative of creating new products from millets. Lending value addition to these grains, they developed items such as cookies, cakes, and muffins, as well as baby food. This led to an increase in the sales of millet-based products and a subsequent rise in the demand for millets themselves.Mr Modi also mentioned Chekjing Sangma, who is a local farmer in the village of Sadolpara, located in the West Garo Hills district of Meghalaya. Recognising the importance of millets, Chekjing Sangma started cultivating them using modern methods. This has not only increased his income but has also fostered greater awareness within the village. Mr Modi also mentioned a village called Kezoma in Kohima, Nagaland, where the cultivation of millets had ceased for over a decade. In 2024, the local community resumed the cultivation of millets. In 2025, Kezoma celebrated its first-ever millet festival. Now, there is a rapidly growing demand for products made from millets in this region as well. The Prime Minister said these examples demonstrate how India’s youth are linking traditional crops with new opportunities, and how villages are advancing on the path to prosperity while preserving their heritage.The birth anniversary of Maharishi Valmiki will be observed tomorrow, on 26th of October. Prime Minister remarked that though thousands of years have passed, Maharishi Valmiki’s Ramayan continues to offer new insights even today. He added that through Ramayan, Maharishi Valmiki has imparted profound life lessons, including the value of persistence, service, compassion and social harmony. Mr Modi said that in the Valmiki Ramayan, the character of Lord Ram serves as a beautiful embodiment of these values. He said Lord Ram embraced the love and devotion of Mata Shabari and honoured his friendship with Nishadraj.Prime Minister stated that the spirit of taking everyone along continues to guide people even today. He said this sentiment is also reflected in the grand Ram Mandir in Ayodhya, where shrines dedicated to Maharishi Valmiki, Nishadraj and Mata Shabari as well have been built. He was pleased to note that the airport in Ayodhya has been named after Maharishi Valmiki. The Prime Minister said the nation will celebrate the 150th birth anniversary of Bhai Parmanand on the 4th of November. He said that Bhai Parmanand’s association with Arya Samaj was a major source of inspiration and ideals for him.  In the very early 20th century, Bhai Parmanand traveled to South Africa for the work of Arya Samaj, where he also met Mahatma Gandhi.He also worked among the ‘Girmitiya’ community in Guyana, which was a significant centre for Arya Samaj at that time. Mr Modi said that during his visit to Guyana, he had the privilege of visiting the Arya Samaj memorial. He said Bhai Parmanand played a major role in the freedom movement. He was also one of the founding members of the Ghadar Party. His influence on the struggle for Independence was so profound that the British authorities sentenced him to ‘Kala Pani’. He authored a book titled ‘Aapbeeti: Kaale Paani Ki Kaaraavaas Kahaani’. Mr Modi termed this book as a must-read to truly understand the sacrifices made by freedom fighters. After completing his sentence, Bhai Parmanand turned his focus towards the field of education, and even taught Bhagat Singh.  In later years, he remained associated with the Hindu Mahasabha for many years. Mr Modi offered homage to Bhai Parmanand and urged the youth to learn about him and inspire others as well.Concluding his Mann Ki Baat address, the Prime Minister extended his best wishes to the people for the upcoming festivals, including Diwali and Chhath. He hoped that people would celebrate these festivals while staying healthy and safe. He also said he is looking forward to receiving messages and suggestions from people for Mann Ki Baat.

. The State Bank of India (SBI) has individually notified customers whose personal data was identified in a recent suspected cyber incident, assuring them that their account balances and funds remain safe. In a statement issued yesterday, the country’s largest public sector lender said, the affected customers have been informed. The bank also advised customers to follow safe digital banking practices and remain alert to suspicious calls, messages and emails. SBI initiated a detailed investigation after receiving alerts on 16th of this month from its Threat Intelligence Service Provider, the Defence Cyber Agency and the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) about suspected customer data exposure on the dark web.A preliminary analysis of around three lakh 75 thousand records identified 3,897 customer records containing personally identifiable information. The information reportedly included names, mobile numbers, email addresses, dates of birth and residential addresses. The bank immediately activated its cyber incident response and containment measures. It also appointed an independent cybersecurity agency empanelled by CERT-In to assess the incident and establish the nature and extent of the suspected data exposure.SBI clarified that the incident had no material impact on its business operations, financial performance or continuity. It said its core banking services continue to function normally without disruption. The bank has urged customers never to share their one-time passwords, PINs or banking passwords with anyone and to exercise caution while responding to unsolicited communications.
